clue.text: Squeak to bring telephone conversation to an end

definitions.meaning: a narrow squeak is a narrow escape, a near thing

definitions.text: bring telephone conversation to an end
definitions.meaning: literally, to finish a phone call by ringing off

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow squeak and a near miss are the same idea, and ending a phone chat is literally shutting the conversation down.

clue.text: Flute used to lure men to sea

definitions.meaning: to flute is to pleat or ridge, as with a goffering iron
the old sense of press-ganging or decoying men into a ship's crew

explanation.definitionFit: To pleat pastry edges or fabric is to flute them, and the press-gang agents who trapped sailors were known by the same verb.

clue.text: Lily's relation accepts good advice from counsel

indicators.note: one piece accepts, i.e. takes inside itself, the other

parts.note: the onion was long classed in the lily family, so it is a relation of the lily
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: A gardener muses on which plants are related to the lily, and a lawyer's advice is sought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' is the container signal. Older botany put onions and garlic in the lily family, hence the relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister's formal written view on a case is called counsel's opinion.

clue.text: Mysterious giant mice on the loose

indicators.note: animals on the loose are running free and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Escaped oversized rodents are a puzzling sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of GIANT and MICE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling and hard to fathom is said to be puzzling or obscure.

clue.text: An expression of dissatisfaction from everyone in good health

parts.note: all means everyone
someone thriving says they are feeling very well

explanation.surface: A doctor finds every patient fit, yet someone still grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said grudgingly: 'that's all very well, but...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a grudging objection, conceding a point before a complaint.

clue.text: Deep blue .

definitions.meaning: a deep voice or note is not high-pitched
feeling blue means feeling down in spirits

explanation.definitionFit: A deep note sits at the bottom of the scale, and blue moods are dejected ones.

clue.text: Among aces, a king

parts.note: mid is a short form of amid, meaning among
in card notation an ace is marked A, so aces are As

explanation.surface: A card player picks out a king from a hand full of aces.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a card hand; the king is the legendary Phrygian ruler whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Phrygian monarch with the golden touch was a ruler of that rank.

clue.text: Love-in-a mist given water

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: The garden flower love-in-a-mist is being watered.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-a-mist is a blue garden flower; the hyphens hide that 'in' tells you to put O inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been watered is damp.

clue.text: Official document turned up among freedom fighters in internment

indicators.note: the fighters are held in internment, enclosed by the other piece
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: amid means among
the PLO, the Palestine Liberation Organization, called itself a body of freedom fighters

explanation.surface: A missing paper surfaces among guerrillas held in a detention camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the word for among, and 'in internment' holds the Palestinian group inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course is a formal certificate issued by an authority.

clue.text: Slip up, entering separate submission

indicators.note: one piece enters, going inside the other

parts.note: to sunder is to separate

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to slip is to make an error, to err

explanation.surface: A mistake made while splitting apart a document handed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip up' reads as a single blunder, but 'up' reverses the error word in this down clue, and 'entering' sends it into the word for separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to an opponent is giving in, a submission.

clue.text: Los Angeles can put in a team that's withdrawn at the start

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the whole run is read backwards
the can is put in, placed inside, the team

parts.note: a team of two is a pair, written II in Roman numerals
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles side is entered in a competition and then pulled out before it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the can inside the pair, and 'that's withdrawn' reverses the whole run. Taking a team as a pair, Roman two, is the least certain step.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming first in a sequence belongs to the beginning.

clue.text: Fancy a little cry

parts.note: a fancy is a whim
per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: A child, on a sudden impulse, sheds a few tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like an article but gives PER, as in so much per head.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, feeble sob or moan is a soft wail.

clue.text: Only half is grasped by school marmish governess

definitions.text: Only half is grasped by school marmish governess

indicators.note: one piece is grasped, held within, by the other

parts.note: a schoolmarmish person is prim

indicators.note: only one half of the little word is kept, its second letter

explanation.surface: A strait-laced governess takes in only half of what she hears.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the second half of 'is', goes inside PRIM. As a whole the clue recalls Mrs General, the governess in Dickens's Little Dorrit, who teaches 'papa, potatoes, poultry, prunes and' this word to shape the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs General, Dickens's governess, prescribes a phrase ending in this word for prim pursed lips, so it is a prim governess's word.

clue.text: Oarsmen — several dance

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
some means several

explanation.surface: A rowing crew and several others take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance is the eightsome reel, a Scottish country dance for eight people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish reel for eight dancers is a lively country dance of that name.

clue.text: Information a couple of chaps get about the French ladies

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: two men is a couple of chaps
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Two men gather facts about the French and their womenfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information. 'about' puts the couple of chaps around the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Women of good breeding were called ladies, the female counterpart of gentlemen.

clue.text: Has the ability to stir

definitions.meaning: the verb meaning is able to

explanation.definitionFit: Being able to do something is the modal verb, while stir and the American slang word both mean jail.

clue.text: A flower-make something up about it

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: to compose is to create or make up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A florist invents a story about a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the verb around 'it'. A daisy is one of these, its head made of many tiny florets.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants of the daisy family, whose heads are clusters of florets, are classed by that botanical name.

clue.text: No sentry had to be ordered to have a shot

indicators.note: letters ordered afresh are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A sentry is told to fire his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven letters of NO SENTRY HAD are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempting something for the first time is making an attempt at it.

clue.text: A threat to planes -Reykjavik's six missing, 100 damaged

indicators.note: the remaining letters are damaged, knocked out of order
the six is missing, taken out

parts.note: the Icelandic capital's name with its S
VI is six in Roman numerals
C is 100 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: At Reykjavik airport six aircraft are lost and a hundred damaged in a terror attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes VI from REYKJAVIKS to leave REYKJAKS; 'damaged' rearranges that with C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes an aircraft in flight is a hijacker, a danger to aviation.

clue.text: Reconstruction of crime — all pay for mystery drama

indicators.note: something reconstructed is built again in a different order

explanation.surface: Police stage a crime reconstruction and everyone is paid for a whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mystery' is not a whodunnit: medieval mystery plays dramatised Bible stories and saints' lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval plays on Bible stories or saints' lives were known as mysteries.

clue.text: Smiling and laughing about commercial

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: riant is an old word, from French, for laughing
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A cheerful advertisement shows people laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the old word for laughing, a rare literary borrowing from French, around the advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaming face glowing with happiness is a smiling one.

clue.text: Some members of a club are lawyers

indicators.note: only some of the letters are taken, from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people in a club are members of the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'cluB ARe'. Barristers collectively are called the Bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers as a body make up the legal profession of that name.

clue.text: Where speech can appear all in favour

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a boon is a favour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone votes yes to a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all in favour' sounds like a vote, but 'in' is the container signal. Comic-strip speech is drawn in a bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: In comics, the words a character speaks are drawn inside a rounded speech bubble.

clue.text: Strange chap — he's joined a society

parts.note: odd means strange
a fellow is a chap

explanation.surface: An eccentric man signs up to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a mutual benefit club; a member is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Oddfellows friendly society is known by that title.

clue.text: She takes the, road into the city

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: A woman drives along the motorway into town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England, and the M1 is Britain's main motorway. 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Any girl's name can stand for 'she', and this is one such name.

clue.text: Share a great deal, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone offers a large portion, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or distribute is to share out portions.

clue.text: It's'included in the benefit of clergy

indicators.note: one piece is included, placed inside, the other

parts.note: taken as written
it, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Something is part of the legal privilege once given to clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' is the container signal. Benefit of clergy was once a legal privilege; here it means the clergy's income, a tenth of produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of farm produce paid to support the parish priest was the clergy's income.

clue.text: Fancy one soldier wearing long hair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the soldier wears the hair, so it goes around him

parts.note: a mane is long hair
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A long-haired soldier is admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means the soldier has the long hair around him.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Amount taken by one 'given short measure

definitions.text: Amount taken by one 'given short measure

parts.words: Amount taken by one 'given short measure
parts.note: the saying 'give him an inch and he'll take' this old cloth measure, about 45 inches

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says give someone an inch and they will take this much more.
explanation.definitionFit: An old cloth measure of about 45 inches is what a greedy person grabs in the proverb after being given an inch.

clue.text: Pretend to understand

definitions.meaning: to claim or suggest falsely, as in 'he made out he was ill'
to discern or grasp, as in 'I can't ... what he means'

explanation.definitionFit: To claim something false is one sense of the phrasal verb; to discern something dimly is another.

clue.text: List of competitors with two, three or four points

parts.note: two points of the compass, east and north
a try in rugby was worth three or four points depending on the era and code

explanation.surface: A competition list explains the scoring system.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, the score for grounding the ball, called a try, has been worth three or four points.
explanation.definitionFit: The roster of those taking part in a race or contest is the field of entrants.

clue.text: Projected into the future, half the capital is applied to farm buildings

indicators.note: only the first half of the city's name is kept

parts.note: London is the capital
a grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings

explanation.surface: Half of London's money is spent on farm buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is applied to' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast covering a long period ahead is a far-reaching one.
